title: RAW: minimum whole-group omissions under a small fixed nucleus-carrier inventory
summary: Extend1042's zero-exception question to an exact optimistic coverage envelope. For K=3,5,7,8 minimize entire uncovered groups and independently uncovered wholeform types over all K-unit representative sets. Lower bounds on required written-nucleus absence, not actual vowel masks or abjad support.

design.mechanism: Every intact nonempty nucleuscarrier over the22workingunits contributes one chosen representativeunit. AtmostKcarriers or common-unit carrierfamilies yield atmostKrepresentatives. Any writtenwholeword avoiding all representatives contains none of the allegedcarriers, so its nucleus must be omitted/implicit or the source/group contract violated.
design.question: How many such exceptions are unavoidable, rather than merely whether zero exceptions is possible?
design.prediction: Minimum uncovered occurrences at K must be positive on GE2 forK<=8 by old1355/1042, but its magnitude and type spread are unknown. Occurrence and type minima are separately optimized and must not be combined into an invented common witness.
design.source: Same1233strict cache, FULLandGE2formsonatleast2physicalleaves. No new rawdata or sounds.1355optimizes erasedSIGNmass underZEROemptygroups, not the present missedWHOLEGROUP objective.
design.decision: If the optimistic bound is small,1042's exact contradiction must not be presented as requiring widespread vowel omission. If substantial, a later phonetic model must pay that many exceptions explicitly. Report continuous bounds, no arbitrary threshold or language-selection decision.
design.limits: A representativehit may come from a consonant, so maximumcoverage is only an upper bound on actualvowelcarriercoverage. No sign meaning, identifiedabbreviation, probability, word-boundary proof or abjadconfirmation. Codeforms mustremain intactandaligned tosameworkingunits; an omitted nucleus is not necessarily a silent vowel in a real source.
